title: Secondary economic activities
competency: Explain manufacturing, construction and power production.

keywords.def: Adding value to products by processing them: manufacturing, construction, power production.
Turning raw materials into products using labour, energy and equipment.
The place (factory) where manufacturing takes place.

en.text: Secondary activities add value to products by changing their form: manufacturing, construction and power production. Manufacturing turns raw materials into products using labour, energy and equipment; an industry (factory) is the place where manufacturing happens.

screens.title: Cotton to cloth
screens.ask: A factory in Kombolcha turns cotton into cloth. What has it added to the cotton?
screens.after: Value. Processing raw cotton into cloth makes it more useful. That is a secondary activity.

screens.title: Secondary economic activities
paras: Secondary activities add value to products by changing their form through processing.
They include manufacturing, construction and power production.
Manufacturing uses machines, tools and labour to make things for use or sale, from handicrafts to high technology.
screens.note: Manufacturing is the activity. Industry is the place (factory) where it happens.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Adding value to products by processing them: manufacturing, construction, power production.

screens.text: What is the difference between manufacturing and industry?
opts: Manufacturing is the activity; industry is the place
Industry is the activity; manufacturing is the place
screens.ans: Manufacturing is the activity; industry is the place
